## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D esports manager inspired by Team Fight Manager, playable on phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Implement the game now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Support responsive layouts and touch controls for mobile devices.
- User requested small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport at most 1280px wide, and reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained browser game in a single HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
- Created an original esports league and team, with roster management, tactics, standings, match drafting, simulation, and season progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive clubhouse dashboard, roster training, strategy settings, league schedule, and standings.
- Implemented champion draft, simulated best-of-three matches, results and rewards, weekly advancement, save persistence, and mobile navigation.
- Verified JavaScript syntax, desktop gameplay flow, and mobile layout with Chromium; no runtime errors and no horizontal overflow.
- Saved and inspected screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/nexus-latest.jpg`.

### Active
- (none)

1. Optionally review `index.html` and make any desired polish changes.
2. Report completion and note the assumptions: original fictional teams and simplified auto-simulated MOBA matches.

- `index.html`: Complete playable game implementation.

- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server was started on port 3002.
- Verification showed 10 schedule fixtures; dashboard standings include 6 teams.

content.text:
Implemented a playable 2D esports manager in `index.html`.

You can manage and train your five-player roster, set tactics, draft champions, watch or skip best-of-three match simulations, earn rewards, and advance through a 10-week season. The interface adapts to phone and tablet screens, with touch-friendly mobile navigation and progress saved in the browser.

Verified the gameplay flow and JavaScript syntax in Chromium. The mobile layout showed no horizontal overflow. A screenshot from the desktop check is saved at `/tmp/opencode/nexus-latest.jpg`.

Assumptions: the league and teams are fictional, and matches use simplified auto-simulation rather than manual gameplay.
